newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Jan jobless to hit 4.6 mln - paper.
newsitem.headline: German Jan jobless to hit 4.6 mln - paper.

text.p: German unemployment surged to a new post-war record in January, rising by a massive 450,000 people from the December total to 4.6 million, newspapers said on Thursday ahead of the release of official data later.

The Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said that the Federal Labour Office, which compiles the figures, had confirmed the unadjusted figure. Officials and trade unionists had earlier predicted a jobless jump to 4.4 million.
The Sueddeutsche said that a cold snap in January, when snow blanketed the country for weeks, had put more outdoor workers, like builders, out of work.
"In January even more builders were sacked and the weather was very cold," an official from the Federal Labour Office told the newspaper.

No figures have yet been mentioned for seasonally adjusted joblessness -- a figure watched by economists because it shows the underlying trend. A Reuters poll showed a consensus forecast for a month-on-month rise of 52,000 in January.

The jobs data are likely to pile the pressure on Chancellor Helmut Kohl to speed up fundamental reforms of the tax and pensions system, over which his three-party conservative coalition is now wrangling.
